title: QVAC diffusion performance evaluation - round two
intro: Completed CUDA research campaign, 29 October 2026. Recommendations below select candidates for the next implementation; they are not production release approval. V means tried, including rejected experiments. X means no defensible speed measurement. Speedup = baseline time / candidate time; percentages describe latency reductions, not quality percentages. R2 native controls already include H3 flash attention, FLUX GEMM VAE and LTX residency. Most R2 screens have one warmup plus one measured request; confirmation runs and fresh-process CLI measurements are labeled separately. Quality is measured against the same-host quantized control, not an original full-precision ground truth.

Official model.

details: Recommended set and directly measured cumulative effect

On the pinned QVAC engine, retain the memory-fitting H3 configuration and use the global-flash profile as the only established speed candidate: RTX 1.057x and Spark 1.091x versus the original control, with small reviewed video differences and exact audio. The isolated upstream fusion experiment is the strongest engine candidate: RTX 1.082x with exact output and Spark 1.138x with tiny video differences comparable to repeated unchanged runs and exact audio. The directly measured RTX fusion-plus-VAE-only-flash combination reaches 1.163x (14.04% less generation latency), with tiny video differences and exact audio; two additional prompts save 14.93% and 15.19%. Spark saves 23.42% (401.45 to 307.42 s, 1.306x) on three repeated runs of one prompt, with tiny video differences and exact audio. Two additional Spark prompt pairs confirm 26.09% and 25.29% lower generation latency, with exact audio. Their video PSNR is 51.94-55.39 dB; each extra prompt has one invocation per variant. A minimal QVAC backport remains required; ablations on both GPUs attribute the useful gain to the H3-specific changes. Do not multiply these gains: on the newer upstream engine, no-global-flash parent to isolated-plus-global-flash measured 105.39 to 89.58 s (1.176x, 15.00% lower), but changed motion and audio (PSNR 23.68 dB, SSIM 0.8472, audio SNR 10.85 dB). That combination fails the visually identical target. On RTX, fusion alone was byte exact against its already-global-flash parent.
Isolated H3 fusions above 5%: scope and risk

The tested upstream experiment retains fused SwiGLU, strided QKV views, partial RoPE and AV input-view changes, plus shared runner and ggml changes, while restoring the parent TransformerBlock projection/modulation layout. RTX paired prompt medians are 96.94 to 89.58 s; two additional prompts each had one invocation per variant: 96.82 to 89.15 s and 96.95 to 90.26 s. All five matched AVI comparisons (ten files) are byte exact including audio. On the repeated prompt, sampled GPU peak falls 17292 to 16892 MiB (-400 MiB, -2.31%); process-tree RSS falls 36.273 to 35.877 GB (-1.09%). These are one-second sampled peaks, not allocator-level guarantees. This result is measured on upstream parent 77b72a2e and an isolated variant of PR #2240, not on a new QVAC engine package. QVAC has custom H3 GGUF/audio handling, so implementation requires a minimal engine backport, temporary addon overlay validation, then the normal engine/registry/addon sequence. No SDK change is indicated.
Approximate reuse above 5%: why it is rejected

EasyCache at 0.20 skips one of eight H3 steps; DBCache/TaylorSeer skip two. Their speedups are real, but fixed-seed video motion/detail and audio waveforms change. The more aggressive modes show visible artifacts on both GPUs. In this pinned engine, the two flags reuse whole condition outputs and produce identical files to each other; they are not validated equivalents of every published block-cache algorithm. The logged warmup counter is not enforced by the inspected before-condition reuse path. No cache implementation fix or default change is proposed from these results.
Upstream repeatability and shared-engine validation

In the Spark confirmation, repeated unchanged parent runs differ at PSNR 52.55-52.90 dB and SSIM 0.99832-0.99841 with exact audio. The isolated candidate versus parent is in the same small-difference range on that prompt: PSNR 52.43-53.07 dB, SSIM 0.99823-0.99850 and exact audio. Two additional prompts give PSNR 55.16 and 52.34 dB with exact audio. The inspected frames show no material visual distinction; this is not a bit-exact guarantee on Spark. Generation medians for the repeated prompt are 341.57 to 300.04 s (12.16% less); the two additional prompt pairs are 342.32 to 301.80 s and 328.21 to 290.04 s. The full PR changes are much larger: PSNR 22.72 dB and audio SNR 6.67 dB against the second parent invocation. The first screening parent timing overlapped task-local CPU conversion; the later confirmations above were collected after conversion. An unrelated-model check also found all-white LTX output on the second invocation of both upstream builds. Consequently an upstream pin update cannot be treated as a validated substitute for a minimal H3 backport.
Cumulative H3 gain: preserve text conditioning

A separate comparison enables flash attention only in diffusion and the VAE, leaving the text encoder unchanged. The RTX parent uses diffusion-only flash; the isolated candidate adds VAE flash. Generation times are 104.18 to 89.55 s for the repeated prompt, 104.89 to 89.23 s for the teapot and 104.70 to 88.80 s for the robot. The first prompt has three fresh-process measurements per side; the other two each have one. The first baseline ran before the user-requested pause; the two additional paired prompts ran after resume and support the same direction. All five audio comparisons are sample exact. Video PSNR is 52.32-56.23 dB and SSIM 0.99878-0.99929; sampled frames, including native-resolution comparisons, show no visible distinction. This is directly measured cumulative performance, not multiplication of individual gains. Scope would include the minimal H3 engine backport and an independent VAE attention setting in the engine/addon. The pinned engine currently exposes global and diffusion-only booleans; the upstream CLI selector is not an existing QVAC request flag. Spark generation medians are 401.45 to 307.42 s (1.306x, 23.42% less) over three fresh processes. Spark PSNR is 52.55-52.70 dB, SSIM 0.99835-0.99840, and all audio samples match. Sampled frames and a native-resolution comparison show no visible distinction. Two additional Spark prompt pairs confirm 26.09% and 25.29% lower generation latency, with exact audio. Their video PSNR is 51.94-55.39 dB; each extra prompt has one invocation per variant. For this combined RTX profile, sampled GPU peak falls 400 MiB (2.31%), while process RSS rises from 35.879 to 36.262 GB (+0.383 GB, +1.07%). Spark process RSS rises from 2.592 to 2.771 GB (+0.179 GB, +6.90%); RSS excludes accelerator allocations and is not total UMA usage. It is therefore a measured speed/quality candidate with a small host-memory trade-off, not an improvement in every metric.
Global flash attention: measured scope

RTX: 120.398 s to 113.872 s. Spark: 659.693 s to 604.903 s. The change is one existing constructor option, flash_attn:true. It selects fused attention in additional engine modules; diffusion_fa:true already selected it for diffusion. VAE medians fell from 25.716 to 19.252 s on RTX and 106.949 to 57.055 s on Spark. No new kernel, engine dependency, SDK API, version or registry pin is required. Baseline/candidate measured ranges were 120.287-120.471 / 113.487-114.108 s on RTX and 651.259-661.465 / 604.847-612.133 s on Spark.
Quality and repeatability

Spark: PSNR 53.67 dB; SSIM 0.998728; pixel RMSE 0.528/255 (0.207% of full range); audio RMSE 0 in float PCM sample units. RTX: PSNR 53.58 dB; SSIM 0.998652; pixel RMSE 0.534/255 (0.209% of full range); audio RMSE 0 in float PCM sample units. All 124 exported frames and 331200 stereo audio sample values per clip were compared. Two additional Spark prompts improved 661.053 to 619.842 s (6.23%) and 667.320 to 611.614 s (8.35%); each is one request, not a repeated timing median. Their PSNR was 52.50 and 46.71 dB, SSIM 0.998533 and 0.997668, with audio still bit exact. Sampled frames remained visually similar; this is not a universal perceptual guarantee.
Memory limits of the H3 result

RTX sampled GPU peak was 23740 versus 23728 MiB and host RSS 40.031 versus 39.406 GB. Spark primary RSS was approximately 5.91 GB in both profiles; the system-wide MemAvailable decline was 44.513 versus 46.466 GB (+4.39%), with background model seeding confounding that proxy. These measurements do not establish exact peak UMA parity. Keep the option explicit until memory is validated with allocator-level measurements and longer clips.
SGLang: faster warm requests, larger integration scope

SGLang Diffusion 0.5.22 produced a 5.17-second clip in a warm median of 172.799 s versus 659.693 s for original resident QVAC (3.82x), or 604.903 s with QVAC attention tuning (3.501x; 71.43% less latency). Load plus the first warmup request was 384.647 versus 611.751 s for attention-tuned QVAC; this is not a disk-cold benchmark. QVAC saved MJPEG/float-PCM AVI, SGLang H.264/AAC MP4. Pixel PSNR 16.26 dB and SSIM 0.5705 describe different realizations and codecs; they do not prove a quality loss or parity. Adopting SGLang requires a separate Python/Torch serving stack. vLLM-Omni also documents H3, but its GGUF plugin has no matched H3 adapter; no vLLM H3 timing is claimed.
Other-model checks and a minimal implementation boundary

The same isolated upstream build also ran FLUX on Spark: three fresh generation times give 11.95 to 11.63 s median (1.028x, 2.68% less), with three byte-identical image pairs. Scaled LTX is approximately neutral: 41.33 to 41.00 s (0.80% less). However, repeated unchanged upstream LTX runs on Spark themselves differ substantially (PSNR 23.63 dB and audio SNR 1.20 dB), so that diagnostic does not establish QVAC-quality parity. Unscaled LTX remains invalid. The next implementation should preserve QVAC's custom paths and backport only the required H3 operations, with backend fallback and full addon tests. The pinned ggml already has SwiGLU; the tested partial-RoPE API needs a focused ggml change or a measured fallback. Metal and Vulkan performance still require their own booked-host validation.

FLUX 3 Image Klein uses a different 5.6B model and Qwen3-VL encoder. Current pinned QVAC engine has no FLUX 3 loader; FLUX.2 results do not validate it. The official distilled model uses 16 steps and recommends prompt upsampling; this is a separate workload and integration path.
details: Recommended set and directly measured cumulative effect

Use the standard decoder with vae_conv_direct:false and resident parameters when the GPU memory budget permits. New three-prompt RTX medians are 8.792/8.815/8.843 to 2.860/2.859/2.851 s: 3.074-3.102x, 67.47-67.76% less latency. Spark medians are 40.956/41.032/41.052 to 15.433/15.433/15.405 s: 2.654-2.665x, 62.32-62.47% less latency. Keep the CPU-parameter GEMM profile as a separate RTX low-VRAM option; it is slower on Spark. GEMM plus the small decoder reaches 3.158-3.176x from direct VAE (68.33-68.52% less), but the decoder adds only 2.35-2.90% beyond GEMM and introduces visible texture/tint changes. Spark cumulative direct-to-small results are 2.726-2.730x (63.32-63.37% less), but the decoder adds only 2.34-2.65% beyond GEMM. Thus the reliable quality-preserving set uses GEMM with the standard decoder; caches, tiling and four-step sampling are not silently included.
New FLUX confirmation and approximate combinations

Standard GEMM versus direct decoding across the new three-prompt RTX run gives PSNR 58.72-60.28 dB, SSIM 0.99935-0.99959 and RMS error 0.247-0.295/255, with maximum channel error 2. Spark gives PSNR 58.65-60.31 dB, SSIM 0.99935-0.99957, RMS error 0.246-0.298/255 and maximum error 3. Each variant is deterministic across its four runs per prompt on each host. The small decoder is 28M rather than 50M parameters and lowers sampled GPU peak by 11.73% versus standard GEMM, but its marginal speed gain is below 3%. DBCache/TaylorSeer reduce denoising work by skipping four of ten steps, giving about 33-35% less incremental latency but visible image changes. Their scope would be request parameters; the small decoder would additionally change the model artefact. Neither belongs in the visually identical default set.
SGLang comparison above 5%: warm throughput versus startup

With the same prompt, 1024 x 1024 size, ten steps and seed, SGLang 0.5.22 completed one warmup and three measured requests on Spark. Warm median request time is 5.993 s versus 15.433 s for the native GEMM profile: 2.575x, 61.17% less latency. Load plus first output is 58.792 s versus 17.602 s: 41.190 s or 234.01% more. The four SGLang images are byte identical to one another, but differ from the native image (PSNR 11.67 dB, SSIM 0.30438). The inspected image is a valid prompt-consistent scene with a different composition. This is not evidence of inferior or equivalent perceptual quality: runtime RNG and numerical computation differ. The harness preserves Q8 DiT blocks through reversible QKV/AdaLN layout conversion, uses BF16-dequantized Q4 text weights, and extends the harness-local weight discovery list to recognize a real GGUF file; the installed runtime source is unchanged. Torch compilation and breakable CUDA graphs are disabled, and conditioning caching is disabled. A Python serving integration and explicit quality acceptance would be separate work. Do not combine this ratio with native VAE gains or claim a controlled SGLang-versus-vLLM ranking from runs collected in different sessions.
GEMM VAE: what changes and why it is faster

Original-round evidence: The exact configuration change is vae_conv_direct:false. Instead of the direct 2D convolution path, the existing engine forms convolution patches with im2col and multiplies them through its matrix backend. On RTX, median VAE time fell from 6237.650 to 273.530 ms (95.61% less), and total request latency from 8.800 to 2.786 s (68.34% less). A later matched three-prompt rerun gave 3.12-3.14x, with byte-identical exported outputs to the first comparison. Spark VAE time fell from 27321.766 to 1719.887 ms (93.70% less), and total latency from 40.841 to 15.324 s (62.48% less). Denoising settings and checkpoint weights are unchanged. This is kernel selection, with no new CUDA kernel. Denoising then accounts for roughly 84-87% of generation time, making it the next bottleneck.
Memory and delay: the trade-off

RTX sampled GPU peak rose from 11356 to 15636 MiB: +4280 MiB (+37.69%). Spark process-tree RSS rose from 1.204 to 2.322 GB (+92.88%); system MemAvailable declined by 13.812 versus 17.779 GB (+28.72% larger decline). RSS is not total UMA allocation, and MemAvailable is a system-wide proxy. One-second sampling may miss short peaks. First-progress time did not improve consistently (RTX photograph 77 to 83 ms); the benefit is time to the actual image. A strict no-memory-regression default is therefore not justified.
A lower-VRAM RTX alternative above 5%

Combine vae_conv_direct:false with params_backend:"cpu". Parameters stay in host memory while computation runs on CUDA. Across three prompts, adjacent direct-VAE resident controls took 8.693-8.785 s; this profile took 3.313-3.320 s (2.62-2.65x, 61.89-62.21% less latency). Sampled GPU peak fell by 3430 MiB, from 11356 to 7926 MiB (-30.20%). Host RSS rose by 6.647 GB, from 2.614 to 9.262 GB (+254.27%); first progress rose from 77-80 to 302-310 ms. All 12 images were byte-exact to resident GEMM, and the repeated resident/direct outputs matched the previously reviewed files by SHA256. The one comparison below therefore covers both GEMM profiles. Scope: two existing configuration options; no engine/SDK change. This is a host-RAM/VRAM trade-off, not a universal default or an 8 GB card capacity claim.
Spark does not benefit from the RTX placement choice

On Spark, moving GEMM parameters to CPU storage increased matched three-prompt medians from 15.254-15.318 s to 15.901-16.038 s (+4.24-4.70% latency). All 12 image pairs remained byte exact. RSS rose from 1.196 to 9.216 GB (+670.60%); the system MemAvailable decline was 16.679 versus 17.002 GB, which also shows no memory saving. Spark uses shared memory, so the RTX discrete-VRAM rationale does not transfer. Keep resident GEMM as the faster Spark option; no cross-hardware placement default is proposed.
Exact-output placement alternative

Changing CPU parameter storage to params_backend:"cuda0" removes transfers while preserving all exported bytes. It recovered 4.10-5.17% on RTX across three prompts, with higher VRAM use. Native residency is already the default, so this only improves an explicitly offloaded configuration; it adds no speed to an already resident one.
Quality: what about 59 dB means

Original-round evidence: Across three RTX text-to-image prompts, PSNR was 59.43-59.82 dB, SSIM 0.999022-0.999585, and pixel RMSE 0.260-0.272 on the 0-255 scale (0.102-0.107% of full range). PSNR = 20 log10(255/RMSE); exactly 59 dB means about 0.29 of one 8-bit level RMS difference. Changed channels were usually off by one level; maximum observed error was three levels. The reviewed images and native crops were visually indistinguishable. This means small numerical differences, not bit-exact output and not a measured percentage of quality loss. There is no universal PSNR threshold for human perception. Perceptual-metric reference.
Broader workloads and family coverage

On Spark, GEMM gave 2.477x at 512 x 512 (9.771 to 3.945 s), 2.429x at 2048 x 1024 (91.268 to 37.582 s), and 2.749x for a batch of two 768 x 768 images (44.781 to 16.288 s per request). Text-to-image PSNR was 59.28-59.89 dB across the extended cases. Image editing improved 1.878x (79.097 to 42.112 s, 46.76% less), with PSNR 49.48 dB, SSIM 0.997690 and RMSE 0.857/255 (0.336% of range); the reviewed result remained visually similar, with isolated errors up to 44 levels. Encoding differences can be amplified through denoising, so the 59 dB finding is not an editing guarantee. Only Klein 4B Q8 was measured. Shared FLUX.2 VAE architecture makes wider FLUX.2 applicability plausible, but 9B, base/dev, FLUX.1 and FLUX 3 remain unvalidated.
Code change scope and alternatives

The feature branch contains the benchmark runner, helper/tests, README and an unapplied H3 research reproduction patch; it does not change production inference. The separate proposal changes ImgStableDiffusion._load() to add vae_conv_direct:false for explicitly selected CUDA FLUX.2 loads when callers have not selected convolution, fallback or precision rules; generated JS and override tests accompany it. That proposal is not promoted: its guard covers more FLUX.2 checkpoints than the tested 4B model, and the memory cost is material. Callers can already opt in with the existing flag. Actual spatial tiling reduced the memory proxy but visibly changed contrast, so it is rejected here. Tile sizes use latent pixels: a 512 setting did not split the tested images and cannot count as tiling validation; actual 32-latent-pixel tiles were tested separately. The official small decoder was tested in round two and remains an optional memory trade-off, as shown in the table.
Why CUDA graphs stay off

With the same GEMM VAE and three prompts, medians increased from 15.254/15.277/15.318 s to 15.578/15.595/15.547 s. All 12 PNG pairs were byte exact. A separate Nsight trace of the same 1024 x 1024, 10-step shape observed actual CUDA graph launches; profiler overhead is excluded from the latency figures. This was a real enabled build, not an environment flag applied to a build compiled without graph support. The repeated warmup-reset messages warrant profiling before further graph work; no engine pin or build default is changed.
Runtime and sampling comparisons above 5%

vLLM-Omni warm median was 6.512 s versus QVAC GEMM 15.324 s (2.353x); load plus the first request was 68.093 versus 17.732 s, so the faster warm path has a startup cost. Images use different RNG/math: PSNR 11.69 dB and SSIM 0.3044 do not measure perceptual parity. Its stack used vLLM 0.32.0, vLLM-Omni 0.1.dev1 and GGUF plugin 0.0.3. The four-step preset changes the trajectory: 15.324 s to 7.396 s (2.072x; 51.74% less latency). Its image is coherent but differs from the ten-step result (PSNR 17.91 dB, SSIM 0.7251); these are deviation metrics, not a quality ranking. SGLang 0.5.22 rejected the original fused-QKV layout. Round two prepared a reversible Q8-block layout conversion, validated every expected transformer weight through its actual GGUF loader, and completed four image requests. The original loader failure remains recorded.

details: Recommended set and directly measured cumulative effect

Keep resident parameters on Spark and CPU-offloaded parameters on the 32 GB RTX card, with the existing tiled decode path for the strict visual tier. For a small visual-change option on tested 97-frame clips, full temporal decoding saves 4.56-5.59% on RTX with exact audio and a modest measured memory increase. A 193-frame RTX confirmation saves 7.06% with exact audio and small video changes. It is not a universal default: subtle texture/contrast differences remain, and larger workloads need capacity validation. No new exact-output >5% warm native LTX gain has been established. Spark residency alone saves 4.97% versus explicit offload with byte-exact output. Adding full temporal decoding saves another 2.90-3.03% across three prompts. The directly measured cumulative change is 39.777 to 36.678 s (1.084x, 7.79% less warm latency) on one prompt; load plus first output falls 56.237 to 42.962 s (23.61% less). This combined profile has small video differences and exact audio; it does not qualify for the strict visual tier. The schedule and 3D-kernel experiments do not currently justify a production change. Spark 193-frame confirmation completed four requests per profile: 74.142 to 70.780 s, 1.047x, 4.53% less latency; video PSNR 46.59 dB, SSIM 0.99714, with exact audio. The initial generation request was 74.439 versus 77.710 s (3.271 s, 4.39% slower), so the warm median does not guarantee a faster first generation. Load plus first output was 86.690 versus 84.112 s, but load time varied substantially with the existing OS/driver cache state and is not attributed to this decode option. Spark process-tree RSS was 5.832 versus 4.574 GB (-1.258 GB, -21.57%); this excludes accelerator allocations and does not establish lower total UMA use.
Full temporal decode: measured scope and change

Set the existing request parameter temporal_tiling:false to decode the complete temporal latent together, avoiding temporal tile overlap work. The RTX confirmation contains three prompts, one warmup and three measured requests per prompt per profile. End-to-end median reductions are 5.59%, 4.56% and 4.87%; VAE time falls from about 3.60-3.62 s to 2.96 s. The first measured request of one full-decode series took 13.807 s; the other two were 12.550/12.551 s, so this is a median throughput benefit, not a tail-latency guarantee. All four outputs within each prompt/profile are byte identical. Across profiles, all 97 frames were compared numerically and audio was sample exact; nine sampled frames per prompt and selected native-resolution frames were inspected. Subtle texture/contrast changes remain. Spark repeats confirm 2.90-3.03% less end-to-end latency across three prompts, with VAE time falling from about 10.0 s to 8.34-8.36 s. Spark video PSNR is 44.15-51.05 dB with exact audio; all four outputs per prompt/profile are byte identical. Its process RSS changes from 5.509 to 5.515 GB (+0.006 GB, +0.11%); this is not total UMA memory. A longer 193-frame RTX clip also completed four requests per profile: median 22.545 to 20.953 s (1.076x, 7.06% less). VAE time falls 7.383 to 5.726 s (22.45% less); video PSNR is 46.39 dB and SSIM 0.99698, with 772800 exact audio sample values. GPU peak rises 20948 to 21348 MiB (+400 MiB, +1.91%) and process RSS 36.204 to 36.597 GB (+0.393 GB, +1.09%). Four outputs per profile are internally byte identical, but cross-profile video is not. Spark 193-frame confirmation completed four requests per profile: 74.142 to 70.780 s, 1.047x, 4.53% less latency; video PSNR 46.59 dB, SSIM 0.99714, with exact audio. The initial generation request was 74.439 versus 77.710 s (3.271 s, 4.39% slower), so the warm median does not guarantee a faster first generation. Load plus first output was 86.690 versus 84.112 s, but load time varied substantially with the existing OS/driver cache state and is not attributed to this decode option. Spark process-tree RSS was 5.832 versus 4.574 GB (-1.258 GB, -21.57%); this excludes accelerator allocations and does not establish lower total UMA use. Scope is a documented optional request profile; no kernel, dependency or SDK change is needed. The measured memory values are one-second samples, not worst-case guarantees.
Distilled schedule: effective parameters matter

The pinned image addon forwards custom_sigmas, but its video handler does not. Native experiments carrying that key therefore repeated the original schedule; their byte equality is not evidence that two schedules are equivalent. A separate upstream CLI test supplied the actual eight-step distilled schedule and changed the generated scene and audio. On RTX, three fresh-process generation medians changed from 29.97 to 30.65 s; process-wall medians changed from 36.325 to 37.079 s. Spark generation medians are 41.60 to 41.51 s, a negligible 0.22% reduction. Neither host shows a reliable speed benefit. The different output is not automatically inferior: schedule correctness and perceptual quality need their own evaluation. Implementing this capability would be an addon change with explicit parameter validation and video forwarding; it is outside the accepted transparent-performance set. SGLang uses the official fixed schedule, so its comparison with the pinned native addon also changes sampling, in addition to runtime and precision.
SGLang comparison above 5%: valid inference with substantial trade-offs

SGLang 0.5.22 completed one warmup and three measured 512 x 320, 97-frame, 24-fps requests at eight steps. Warm times were 12.784, 12.578 and 12.480 s: median 12.578 s versus native resident QVAC 37.802 s (3.005x, 66.73% less latency). Load plus first output took 326.362 s versus 44.075 s: +282.287 s, +640.47%. Peak PyTorch reserved memory was 68336 MiB (66.73 GiB); this is not directly comparable to native Spark RSS and does not establish an RTX 32 GB fit. The fallback expands the default quantized DiT, encoder and connector values into BF16 files. It uses the official distilled sigma sequence and a harness configuration selecting plain unguided sampling while preserving the explicit LTX-2.3 pipeline architecture. The installed SGLang source is unchanged. All 97 frames decode, and inspected frames show a coherent claymation cat playing piano, with a different scene from QVAC. Cross-runtime PSNR 10.74 dB and SSIM 0.39096 are deviation diagnostics, not a quality ranking. Audio is finite and unclipped; AAC decodes to 384960 sample values versus native PCM 388800, so sample equality is not claimed. Two repeated SGLang outputs have identical decoded video but small audio differences (43.15 dB SNR). The runtime forced its worker to terminate during shutdown and reported one leaked semaphore despite an overall zero exit code. Production use needs lifecycle and memory validation, more prompts and an independent perceptual/audio study. This serving-stack experiment is not included in the recommended native change set.
Attention and temporal decode experiments

Original-round evidence: Global flash: RTX 13.272 s to 13.265 s; Spark 37.879 s to 38.602 s. Full temporal decode on Spark: 37.879 s to 37.096 s. These use existing options, not new engine kernels. A setting is eligible only if its measured speed, output and memory satisfy the selected quality tier; the measured effects and final recommendation must be read together.
Video and audio quality

Original-round evidence: Global flash, Spark: Video bit exact: MAE 0/255, 0% changed values, SSIM 1; audio RMSE 0 in float PCM sample units. Global flash, RTX: Video bit exact: MAE 0/255, 0% changed values, SSIM 1; audio RMSE 0 in float PCM sample units. Full temporal decode, Spark: PSNR 48.40 dB; SSIM 0.997254; pixel RMSE 0.969/255 (0.380% of full range); audio RMSE 0 in float PCM sample units. Exact output for placement tuning was checked across all 12 exported AVI pairs from three prompts, including audio.

validation: Branches only; no PRs. The benchmark branch and isolated CUDA-VAE proposal remain separate. The benchmark branch was refreshed from upstream main be6aba5a7, including diffusion-cpp 0.32.1 and engine package 2026-08-11#8. Native performance measurements use the recorded 0.31.0 addon and engine 4ec33ca2 (#7); they are not relabeled as measurements of the new release. The upstream #8 engine change adds per-device memory-fit reporting; it is distinct from the experimental H3 kernels. No additional production engine pin, SDK API, package dependency, version or changelog change is proposed by this research report.

Validation status: benchmark code revision e9b06f3e0 includes the upstream merge and H3 experimental reproduction patch. It passed 137 Bare tests (519 assertions), 54 Node tests, lint and type checks; lint retains 69 existing JavaScript warnings. The full workflow for this revision passed all 37 executed jobs; 14 unrelated or conditional workflow jobs were skipped by the existing routing. Previous head e7c19f4d2 passed all 37 jobs. This CI validates the benchmark changes and unchanged addon; experimental upstream binaries are validated separately on the booked hosts. The separately isolated default proposal has prior passing validation. The separate proposal head is a47bce0daa6825777a573af8551c1dd27878b085; its earlier 37-job workflow passed, but it has not been refreshed or revalidated for this new release. No existing tests were deleted, disabled or weakened; no AWS Device Farm runs were used.

Coverage: CUDA performance was measured on RTX 5090 (32 GiB-class discrete VRAM) and DGX Spark GB10 (128 GB-class shared memory). CI correctness on another GPU or a Mac does not establish inference performance on M3 Ultra/Pro or Strix Halo. Those measurements remain outstanding.

Reproduction: addon 0.31.0; engine 4ec33ca21eec64b9778b6fd16d58e88cd501936d; ggml 9f94f330ac196e0a2e3176e798b36226b22091a5. All within-host A/B pairs use identical checkpoint hashes and workloads. The RTX and Spark FLUX Q8 files come from different conversions, so absolute cross-host times are not a controlled hardware comparison. Model transfer/load is separate from generation. Different runtime codecs, RNG and precision paths are identified above.

Acceptance: no automatic default is promoted on the strength of these runs. A requirement for zero regression in every metric is not yet met: fast settings have memory, progress-delay or numerical-output trade-offs, and M3/Strix inference performance is unmeasured. The benchmark feature branch contains tooling and an unapplied experimental H3 reproduction patch; production inference behavior is unchanged. Rejected builds and visible tiling deviations stay rejected. Cross-runtime output differences need an independent perceptual/prompt-adherence study; PSNR between different generated realizations is not a quality ranking.

Reproduction bundle: sanitized benchmark JSON inputs and checkpoint SHA256 identities accompany the report. They contain no model weights, host connection details or credentials. Use the feature branch runner and select the permitted physical GPU externally; the inputs use its logical CUDA index.

Branch readiness and next validation: codex/diffusion-performance is validated benchmark infrastructure and an unapplied research patch, not a production H3 backport. Its measured CUDA candidates are ready to guide the next implementation and Mac Studio investigation; it is not evidence of Metal or Strix performance. On Mac Studio, first establish the same-checkpoint Metal baseline on the current QVAC revision, then compare applicable options with repeated cold/warm latency, first output, memory, and video/audio or image quality checks. Cover multiple prompts, image sizes, image editing where supported, and short/long clips. CUDA-only settings must preserve the Metal path. For H3, implement the focused engine backport and required ggml operations with backend fallbacks, then validate through a temporary addon overlay while preserving QVAC-specific loading/audio behavior. Re-run CUDA controls on that exact implementation revision before claiming the research gains survived integration. After Mac and CUDA acceptance, prepare same-repository PRs and run the complete existing desktop build/unit/integration matrix, including Vulkan correctness. Use the engine, separate registry-pin, then addon sequence if those layers change. A later addon release/version/changelog PR remains separate. No PR is opened in this research step.

R2 execution limits: RTX LTX follow-ups resumed after verified QVAC registry downloads. Fully resident weights failed allocation on the 32 GB card; RTX uses CPU-offloaded parameters for the paired control. H3, FLUX and 97-frame LTX three-prompt confirmations are complete on both hosts, together with the H3 combinations, shared-code ablations, stateful decoder checks and 193-frame LTX follow-ups. Preparatory CPU conversion overlapped initial upstream screening; the repeated H3 confirmations were collected after conversion. Such screens are not used as final repeated-performance evidence. The final reruns used ordinary local checkpoint files in the dedicated test directory.

Source-only elimination: GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ does not introduce a new dispatch path for these supported quantized tensors on Blackwell: the inspected pinned ggml already selects MMQ when Turing-or-newer tensor-core instructions are available. No additional build or speed claim is made for that flag. Numerical-scaling diagnostics follow the upstream troubleshooting guidance; white output alone does not prove the root cause.

Final branch check: the unchanged full workflow for revision 5dc725f58b passed all 37 executed jobs; 14 existing conditional jobs were skipped by workflow routing. Subsequent evidence-only documentation commits are checked for JSON validity, reproduction-input schema, content hashes and private-data exclusion; they do not change production or benchmark code.

CI reliability observation: the first Windows Vulkan integration attempt failed the FLUX Klein surjective-fusion test with vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost. No production addon, benchmark code or engine pin changed from the previously passing revision; this does not establish the cause of the device failure. The initial full workflow finished with 35 successful jobs, the Windows integration failure and its dependent merge guard failure. The unchanged failed-job retry passed all 98 Windows integration tests, including the previously failing fusion case. The full workflow then finished successfully with 37 executed jobs passed and 14 existing conditional jobs skipped. No tests, workflow settings or production code were altered for the retry; the initial device-loss cause remains unconfirmed. The failure remains recorded, and no test is disabled or weakened. A clean Mac Studio performance result and exact-implementation CUDA regression checks remain required before promotion.

Research preservation and host release: generated outputs and raw evidence were copied locally and verified by SHA256 before cleanup. The feature branch preserves sanitized reproduction inputs, measurements, quality results, source identities and the experimental patch. Only the dedicated task directory on each host was removed; unrelated files were outside the cleanup scope. No PR has been opened. The share bundle excludes model weights, private raw logs, credentials and host connection details.

Media integrity audit: 530 output files (125 unique contents) were checked for valid, nondegenerate images/video and finite audio. 23 invalid clips belong to the rejected unscaled upstream LTX experiments. Media validity alone is not quality parity; the separate paired metrics, repeatability checks and inspected frames support the quality labels in the tables.

Still unvalidated: performance on M3 Ultra/Pro and Strix Halo; the focused H3 backport on the current QVAC package; H3 reference/image-conditioned modes and longer clips; other FLUX.2 checkpoints and FLUX 3; LTX-2.5; production-resolution LTX memory limits; NVFP4 encoder cold-start/long-prompt benefits; vLLM/SGLang profiles on RTX; cross-runtime perceptual/audio parity and serving lifecycle reliability. The three-repeat confirmations establish useful median trends but do not provide production tail-latency or worst-case-memory guarantees. Fresh-process startup observations include the existing OS and driver cache state; controlled cold-start distributions remain unmeasured. A CUDA-only option must leave Metal/Vulkan behavior intact, and shared engine changes require matched controls on every supported backend before promotion.
